"""Compile the RSS10 record-hardening roles with bounded exact evidence."""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import shutil
import signal
import subprocess
import tempfile
import time
import tomllib

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PACK = ROOT / "RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone"
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
parser.add_argument("--proof", type=Path, required=True)
parser.add_argument("--source-kind", choices=["checkout","exported-workspace"], default="checkout")
args = parser.parse_args()
args.proof = args.proof.resolve()
assert not args.proof.exists()
assert os.getuid() != 0 and os.uname().sysname == "Linux" and os.uname().machine == "x86_64"
OUT = args.proof.parent
OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
commands = []


def sha(raw):
    return hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()


def stop(signum, _frame):
    raise SystemExit(128 + signum)


signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)
signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)


def run(command, cwd, label, expected=0, env=None, timeout=120):
    entry = dict(parentTaskId="rust-capstone-evidence", parentPid=os.getpid(),
                 command=[os.fsdecode(value) for value in command], cwd=str(cwd),
                 startTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(), timeoutSeconds=timeout)
    start = time.monotonic()
    child = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                             stderr=subprocess.PIPE, start_new_session=True)
    entry["pid"] = child.pid
    with (OUT / "processes.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
        stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="start")) + "\n")
    stdout, stderr, cleanup = b"", b"", "owned process exited"
    try:
        stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=timeout)
    except BaseException:
        if child.poll() is None:
            os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate(timeout=3)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                os.killpg(child.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
                stdout, stderr = child.communicate()
        cleanup = "owned process group terminated and reaped"
        raise
    finally:
        with (OUT / "processes.jsonl").open("a") as stream:
            stream.write(json.dumps(dict(entry, event="end", endTime=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).isoformat(),
                                         exitCode=child.returncode, childProcessGroupCleanup=cleanup)) + "\n")
        (OUT / (label + ".stdout.txt")).write_bytes(stdout)
        (OUT / (label + ".stderr.txt")).write_bytes(stderr)
    assert child.returncode == expected, (label, child.returncode, stderr.decode(errors="replace"))
    commands.append(dict(label=label, exitCode=child.returncode, elapsedSeconds=time.monotonic()-start,
                         timeoutSeconds=timeout, stdoutSha256=sha(stdout), stderrSha256=sha(stderr)))
    return stdout, stderr


def verify_committed_bytes(actual, source):
    # Compare raw bytes with the selected commit, independently of the index,
    # clean filters, timestamps, and assume-unchanged flags.
    listing=run(["git","ls-tree","-rz","--full-tree",actual,"--",*source],ROOT,"committed-source-objects")[0]
    entries={}
    for row in listing.split(b"\0"):
        if not row:
            continue
        header,name=row.split(b"\t",1)
        mode,kind,identity=header.split()
        assert mode in [b"100644",b"100755"] and kind==b"blob"
        name=name.decode()
        assert name not in entries
        entries[name]=identity.decode()
    assert entries.keys()==source.keys(),"Committed source paths differ"
    for name,raw in source.items():
        identity=hashlib.sha1(b"blob "+str(len(raw)).encode()+b"\0"+raw).hexdigest()
        assert identity==entries[name],"Source bytes differ from committed revision: "+name
    return entries



import re

claimed=os.environ['SOURCE_REVISION']
assert len(claimed)==40 and all(c in '0123456789abcdef' for c in claimed)
role_names=['Cargo.toml','Cargo.lock','src/lib.rs','src/main.rs','src/fixtures.rs','observations.md']
tool_names=['test/verify_rust_capstone.py','test/verify_rust_capstone_export.py','.github/workflows/rust-capstone.yml']
expected_names=sorted([PACK.name+'/README.md']+[PACK.name+'/'+role+'/'+name for role in ['starter','solution'] for name in role_names]+tool_names)
assert len(expected_names)==16
actual=None
if args.source_kind=='checkout':
    actual=run(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],ROOT,'actual-source-revision')[0].decode().strip()
    assert actual==claimed
    names=run(['git','ls-files','--',PACK.name,*tool_names],ROOT,'source-inventory')[0].decode().splitlines()
    assert names==expected_names
else:
    names=expected_names
for name in names:
    cursor=ROOT
    for part in Path(name).parts:
        cursor=cursor/part
        assert not cursor.is_symlink(),'Linked source entry: '+name
    assert cursor.is_file(),'Missing source entry: '+name
package_files={name.removeprefix(PACK.name+'/') for name in names if name.startswith(PACK.name+'/')}
package_dirs={Path('.')}
for name in package_files:package_dirs.update(Path(name).parents)
for relative in package_dirs:
    offset=0 if str(relative)=='.' else len(relative.parts)
    children={Path(name).parts[offset] for name in package_files if Path(name).is_relative_to(relative) and len(Path(name).parts)>offset}
    assert {p.name for p in (PACK/relative).iterdir()}==children
source={name:(ROOT/name).read_bytes() for name in names}
assert all(b'\r' not in raw for raw in source.values())
committed=verify_committed_bytes(actual,source) if args.source_kind=='checkout' else None
for name,raw in source.items():
    path=OUT/'source'/name;path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);path.write_bytes(raw)
versions={name:run(command,ROOT,name)[0].decode().strip() for name,command in [
    ('rustc',['rustc','--version','--verbose']),('cargo',['cargo','--version']),
    ('rustfmt',['rustfmt','--version']),('clippy',['cargo','clippy','--version'])]}
assert versions['rustc'].startswith('rustc 1.97.1 ')
cases={'cat':[3,99,97,116,1],'empty-label':[0,1],'over-label':[11]+[97]*11+[1],
       'short':[3,99,97],'utf8':[3,255,255,255,1],'kind':[3,99,97,116,9],
       'trailing':[3,99,97,116,1,0],'declared-max':[255],'empty':[],
       'missing-kind':[1,97],'length-only':[11],'unicode':[3,226,152,131,2],
       'exact-max':[10]+list(b'abcdefghij')+[3],'combined':[1,255,9,0]}
assert len(cases)==14


def oracle(values,role):
    data=bytes(values)
    if len(data)>12:error='too-large'
    elif not data:error='empty'
    elif data[0]==0:error='empty-label'
    elif data[0]>10:error='label-too-long'
    elif len(data)<1+data[0]:error='truncated-label'
    elif len(data)==1+data[0]:error='missing-kind'
    elif len(data)>2+data[0]:error='trailing-data'
    else:
        label=data[1:1+data[0]]
        try:label.decode('utf-8')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:error='invalid-utf8'
        else:
            if data[-1] not in [1,2,3]:error='unsupported-kind'
            else:return 'ok:'+str(data[-1])+':'+label.hex()
    return 'error:'+('unclassified' if role=='starter' and error!='too-large' else error)


corpus=[list(values) for length in range(5) for values in itertools.product([0,1,3,255],repeat=length)]
corpus.extend([length]+[value]*length+[kind] for length in range(1,11) for value in [0,97] for kind in [1,2,3])
corpus.extend(cases.values())
corpus=list(map(list,dict.fromkeys(map(tuple,corpus))))
assert 350<len(corpus)<500 and all(len(values)<=13 for values in corpus)
usage=[[],['--case'],['--help','extra'],['--case','cat','extra'],['--case','cat','extra','more'],['--unknown'],['cat'],['--case','unknown']]
USAGE=b'usage: record_hardening_lab --help | --case NAME\n'
roles=[]
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='rust-capstone-native-') as directory:
    work=Path(directory)
    for role,unit_count in [('starter',7),('solution',13)]:
        selected=PACK/role;project=work/role
        shutil.copytree(selected,project)
        original={p.relative_to(project):p.read_bytes() for p in project.rglob('*') if p.is_file()}
        assert tomllib.loads((project/'Cargo.toml').read_text())=={'package':{'name':'record_hardening_lab','version':'1.0.0','edition':'2024'}}
        assert tomllib.loads((project/'Cargo.lock').read_text())['package']==[{'name':'record_hardening_lab','version':'1.0.0'}]
        assert len(re.findall(rb'#\[test\]\s+fn ',source[PACK.name+'/'+role+'/src/lib.rs']))==unit_count
        env={**os.environ,'CARGO_NET_OFFLINE':'true','CARGO_TARGET_DIR':str(work/(role+'-target'))}
        run(['cargo','fmt','--all','--check'],project,role+'-format',env=env)
        run(['cargo','clippy','--locked','--offline','--all-targets','--','-D','warnings'],project,role+'-clippy',env=env)
        out,_=run(['cargo','test','--locked','--offline'],project,role+'-tests',env=env)
        assert f'{unit_count} passed; 0 failed'.encode() in out
        run(['cargo','build','--locked','--offline'],project,role+'-build',env=env)
        binary=Path(env['CARGO_TARGET_DIR'])/'debug/record_hardening_lab'
        assert run([str(binary),'--help'],work,role+'-help',env=env,timeout=30)==(USAGE,b'')
        for repeat in range(2):
            for name,values in cases.items():
                result=oracle(values,role)
                expected=(b'',('error='+result.removeprefix('error:')+'\n').encode(),65) if result.startswith('error:') else (('kind='+result.split(':')[1]+' label-bytes='+str(values[0])+'\n').encode(),b'',0)
                assert run([str(binary),'--case',name],work,f'{role}-case-{name}-{repeat}',expected=expected[2],env=env,timeout=30)==expected[:2]
        for index,arguments in enumerate(usage):
            assert run([str(binary),*arguments],work,f'{role}-usage-{index}',expected=64,env=env,timeout=30)==(b'',USAGE)
        for index,arguments in enumerate([[b'--case',b'\xff'],[b'\xff']]):
            assert run([os.fsencode(binary),*arguments],work,f'{role}-utf8-{index}',expected=64,env=env,timeout=30)==(b'',USAGE)
        driver=['use record_hardening_lab::{parse_record, Record, ParseError};',
                'fn show(value: Result<Record, ParseError>) -> String { match value { Ok(record) => { let hex: String = record.label().as_bytes().iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}")).collect(); format!("ok:{}:{hex}",record.kind().value()) }, Err(error) => format!("error:{}",error.code()) } }',
                'fn main() {']
        expected_rows=[]
        for index,values in enumerate(corpus):
            driver.append('println!("case='+str(index)+' {}", show(parse_record(&['+','.join(map(str,values))+'])));')
            expected_rows.append('case='+str(index)+' '+oracle(values,role))
        driver.append('}')
        consumer=work/(role+'-consumer');(consumer/'src').mkdir(parents=True)
        generated={'Cargo.toml':'[package]\nname = "record_contract_consumer"\nversion = "1.0.0"\nedition = "2024"\n\n[dependencies]\nrecord_hardening_lab = { path = "../'+role+'" }\n',
                   'Cargo.lock':'# This file is automatically @generated by Cargo.\n# It is not intended for manual editing.\nversion = 4\n\n[[package]]\nname = "record_contract_consumer"\nversion = "1.0.0"\ndependencies = [\n "record_hardening_lab",\n]\n\n[[package]]\nname = "record_hardening_lab"\nversion = "1.0.0"\n',
                   'src/main.rs':'\n'.join(driver)+'\n'}
        for name,text in generated.items():
            (consumer/name).write_text(text)
            path=OUT/('generated-'+role)/name;path.parent.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True);path.write_text(text)
        consumer_env={**env,'CARGO_TARGET_DIR':str(work/(role+'-consumer-target'))}
        run(['cargo','build','--locked','--offline'],consumer,role+'-consumer-build',env=consumer_env)
        out,err=run([str(Path(consumer_env['CARGO_TARGET_DIR'])/'debug/record_contract_consumer')],work,role+'-consumer-run',env=consumer_env,timeout=30)
        assert not err and out.decode().splitlines()==expected_rows
        run(['cargo','clean'],project,role+'-clean',env=env)
        out,_=run(['cargo','test','--locked','--offline'],project,role+'-clean-tests',env=env)
        assert f'{unit_count} passed; 0 failed'.encode() in out
        run(['cargo','build','--locked','--offline'],project,role+'-clean-build',env=env)
        assert run([str(binary),'--case','cat'],work,role+'-clean-valid',env=env,timeout=30)==(b'kind=1 label-bytes=3\n',b'')
        assert {p.relative_to(project):p.read_bytes() for p in project.rglob('*') if p.is_file()}==original
        (OUT/role).mkdir();(OUT/role/'record_hardening_lab').write_bytes(binary.read_bytes())
        roles.append(dict(role=role,unitTests=unit_count,unitTestsBeforeAndAfterClean=True,sourceAndLockUnchanged=True,
                          cliCases=28,usageRefusals=10,consumerCases=len(corpus),consumerRows=expected_rows,
                          executableSha256=sha(binary.read_bytes()),generatedDriver={name:sha(text.encode()) for name,text in generated.items()}))
assert not work.exists() and all((ROOT/name).read_bytes()==raw for name,raw in source.items())
assert len(commands)==(105 if args.source_kind=='checkout' else 102)
proof=dict(sourceRevision=actual,checkedOutRevision=actual,baseSourceRevision=claimed,sourceKind=args.source_kind,
           sourceDiscovery='git-index' if args.source_kind=='checkout' else 'fixed-filesystem',
           repositoryCIProvenanceClaimed=args.source_kind=='checkout',committedSourceObjects=committed,
           sourceFiles={name:sha(raw) for name,raw in source.items()},compilerVersions=versions,nativeExecuted=True,
           ordinaryUser=True,allSourceFilesUnchanged=True,temporarySourceCleanup=True,
           noExternalProjectCrates=True,projectChecksOffline=True,legacyPseudocodeNotExecuted=True,
           worksheetCompletionNotInferred=True,allExecutionsNotProven=True,roles=roles,corpus=corpus,commands=commands)
args.proof.write_text(json.dumps(proof,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps(dict(accepted=True,sourceKind=args.source_kind,commands=len(commands),consumerCases=len(corpus)*2,proof=str(args.proof))))

    entries={}
    for row in listing.split(b"\0"):

actual=run(['git','rev-parse','HEAD'],ROOT,'actual-source-revision')[0].decode().strip()

assert not packet.exists() and all((ROOT/name).read_bytes()==raw for name,raw in source.items())
assert len(commands)==7
proof=dict(sourceRevision=actual,checkedOutRevision=actual,sourceKind='checkout',ordinaryUser=True,
           committedSourceObjects=committed,dirtyCheckoutRefusals=dirty_refusals,
           sourceFiles={name:sha(raw) for name,raw in source.items()},allSourceFilesUnchanged=True,
           temporarySourceCleanup=True,gitFreePacketValidated=True,exportedNativeCommands=102,

           exportedCheckoutRevision=None,exportedRepositoryCIProvenanceClaimed=False,
           checkoutModeWithoutGitRefused=True,allRoleNativeChecksRepeated=True,actualIDEIntegrationNotInferred=True,
           commands=commands)

RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone/README.content:
# Legacy record tool hardening

Preserve the supplied record format while replacing the legacy memory operations
with a bounded, owned Rust model. The runnable starter already preserves every
valid record and safely combines most malformed cases as `unclassified`. Its
unfinished work is to classify failures, justify precedence and build the final
review packet. The reference demonstrates one complete design.

## Original course brief

<details>
<summary>Preserved brief for comparison</summary>

````text
## Legacy Tool Hardening Capstone Case

Legacy pseudocode:

```c
int parse_record(const unsigned char *input, size_t length, Record *out) {
	unsigned char declared = input[0];
	char label[12];
	memcpy(label, input + 1, declared);
	label[declared] = '\0';
	out->kind = input[declared + 1];
	out->label = duplicate(label);
	return 0;
}
```

Valid behavior:

- record is one length byte, that many UTF-8 label bytes, and one kind byte;
- label length is 1 through 10 bytes;
- supported kinds are `1`, `2`, and `3`;
- output owns its label;
- trailing bytes are rejected.

Regression corpus:

```text
[3, 99, 97, 116, 1]
[0, 1]
[11, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 97, 1]
[3, 99, 97]
[3, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, 1]
[3, 99, 97, 116, 9]
[3, 99, 97, 116, 1, 0]
[255]
```

Produce a behavior contract, threat model, Rust 2024 data model, bounded parser, typed errors, test matrix, dependency and lock review, and before-and-after claim table. Keep the implementation safe unless an optional supplied ABI adapter creates a genuine need for a narrow unsafe boundary. For advanced evidence, use either the supplied Miri and fuzz summaries or a fixed local run with explicit case, time, input-size, artifact, stop, and cleanup limits.
````

</details>

## Current project route

Use the safe starter, reference implementation and native fixed-corpus record
in `solution/observations.md`. Advanced evidence uses that deterministic native
corpus or the bounded mutation experiment below. The archived brief's optional
Miri/fuzz summaries and ABI adapter were not supplied; they are not prerequisites
or promised artifacts for this implementation.


## Concrete Rust contract

`parse_record(&[u8])` returns an owned `Record` or a typed error. `Record` fields
are private; accessors expose a borrowed label and a copied kind. Label length
means UTF-8 bytes. NUL and other valid UTF-8 scalar values are permitted by this
original format; do not silently invent a printable-only rule.

Check in this order: more than 12 total bytes; empty input; zero declared length;
declared length above 10; truncated label; missing kind; trailing data; invalid
UTF-8; unsupported kind. This order makes combined faults deterministic. For
example the supplied 11-byte label record has 13 total bytes and is `too-large`;
`[11]` is `label-too-long`. `[1,255,9,0]` is `trailing-data` before encoding or
kind checks. Only the successful result allocates its owned label, at most 10
bytes. The caller already owns the input slice; this API does not bound an
allocation made by a caller before invoking it.

The reference codes are `too-large`, `empty`, `empty-label`, `label-too-long`,
`truncated-label`, `missing-kind`, `trailing-data`, `invalid-utf8`, and
`unsupported-kind`. The starter reports `too-large` for oversized input and
`unclassified` for the other malformed cases. Neither role panics on supplied
malformed input, returns a partially populated record or echoes input in errors.

## Core project: four vertical slices

1. Predict all eight original corpus results. Annotate every unchecked legacy
   read, copy, terminator write and ownership ambiguity without executing it.
   Record the valid grammar, caller trust and 12-byte accepted record bound.
2. Inspect the safe baseline. Preserve all valid behavior and its owned result.
   Introduce distinct errors and the stated precedence. Keep all fallible work
   before constructing the record. Add one focused regression per failure.
3. Test combined faults, three-byte Unicode, exact bounds and output ownership
   after mutating/dropping the source. Separate format, lint, compile, ordinary
   tests and independently generated corpus observations in the evidence table.
4. Finish `observations.md` with a threat model, before/after claim table,
   dependency/lock review, residual risks and a five-minute reproduction packet.

## Choice and challenge work

Choose one: generate valid labels for all three kinds and compare both roles;
or add a diagnostic-only formatter that escapes label bytes without changing the
parser grammar. For the challenge, mutate the fixed corpus with explicit bounds:
at most 4096 cases, each at most 13 bytes, one native process, a 30-second external
timeout, and no filesystem/network input. Record the seed/case list, counts,
stop rule and temporary-file cleanup. A deterministic bounded corpus is valid
evidence; random fuzzing and extra tool installation are optional.

This parser needs neither unsafe nor concurrency. The ledger should justify
their absence. Do not add an ABI adapter or workers merely to tick a box. If an
optional extension genuinely requires either, carry forward its separate memory
contract or work/cancellation invariant and limit claims to observed evidence.

## Reproduction

From either selected package, using Rust/Cargo 1.97.1 and Edition 2024:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --locked --offline --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case cat
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case unicode
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case trailing
```

The first two runs return 0 with `kind=1 label-bytes=3` and
`kind=2 label-bytes=3`, respectively. The trailing case returns 65 with empty
stdout and `error=unclassified` (starter) or `error=trailing-data` (reference) on
stderr. Every line ends with one newline. Run the last command separately when
using a shell that stops on nonzero status; the refusal is an expected result.

Use exactly `--help` or `--case NAME`. The fixed names are `cat`, `empty-label`,
`over-label`, `short`, `utf8`, `kind`, `trailing`, `declared-max`, `empty`,
`missing-kind`, `length-only`, `unicode`, `exact-max` and `combined`. Unknown,
missing, extra or non-UTF-8 arguments return 64 with the usage line only on
stderr. Help prints it on stdout and returns 0. The executable selects only
compiled fictional fixtures, does not open a supplied path and prints metadata
for valid records, never their full labels.

## Review limits and recovery

The manifest and lock select no external project crates. Record that fact and
the actual compiler, but do not turn it into a claim that the toolchain or this
program has no vulnerabilities. Tests and the fixed corpus prove selected
behavior. Safe Rust removes the demonstrated unchecked-memory path here;
grammar mistakes, resource use in a future caller, dependencies in an extension,
operational controls and future changes still need review. No whole-program
security, production activation, fuzzing or Miri run is implied.

Keep the original reading and starter separate from an edited attempt. To
reproduce a clean comparison, export or copy the selected package and retain

name = "record_hardening_lab"
version = "1.0.0"

# Reference capstone evidence packet

This packet describes the supplied implementation and the native observations
recorded at source `5b8ed5bcb87702644e8ac277f1f0d1467fee005d`. The reference's
Rust and Cargo files are unchanged by this completed reading. An edited program
needs its own observations.

## Original contract and failure ledger

One byte declares 1 through 10 UTF-8 label bytes, followed by exactly one kind
byte in `1`, `2`, `3`. A successful result owns the complete label. Empty labels,
unsupported kinds and trailing bytes are outside the valid grammar. Label
length counts bytes; NUL and control scalars are not excluded by that grammar.
The original C pseudocode is reviewed text and was never executed.

| Original input | Reference result | Legacy diagnosis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `[3,99,97,116,1]` | kind 1, owned `cat` | The accesses fit this particular input, but the function still lacks explicit error and allocation-ownership contracts. |
| `[0,1]` | `empty-label` | The old code accepts an empty label, violating the declared grammar even though these accesses fit. |
| `[11,97,97,97,97,97,97,97,97,97,97,97,1]` | `too-large` | This record has 13 total bytes, above the 12-byte maximum. The old code accepts an out-of-contract length; copying 11 bytes and writing index 11 happen to fit its 12-byte local array. |
| `[3,99,97]` | `truncated-label` | The three-byte copy reads beyond the supplied two label bytes; the subsequent kind read is also outside the input. |
| `[3,255,255,255,1]` | `invalid-utf8` | The accesses fit, but the old function never validates encoding. |
| `[3,99,97,116,9]` | `unsupported-kind` | The old function accepts an unsupported kind. |
| `[3,99,97,116,1,0]` | `trailing-data` | The old function ignores the final byte instead of requiring exact consumption. |
| `[255]` | `label-too-long` | The old copy reads outside input and exceeds local label capacity; the terminator and kind accesses are also out of bounds. |

Empty input adds an unchecked `input[0]` read. A declared length of 12 would
place the terminator at index 12, beyond the local array, even if the copied
bytes fit. The old `length` parameter is ignored. The shown byte-sized length
alone does not establish `size_t` arithmetic overflow on the tested platform;
the demonstrated failures are missing bounds, grammar and ownership checks.
The behavior of `duplicate`, allocation failure and responsibility for freeing
its result are unspecified by the pseudocode.

## Threat model and boundaries

The parser receives a caller-owned immutable byte slice. Its trust boundary is
the first interpretation of untrusted bytes as a record. The caller may supply
any byte values or length. The parser rejects total length above 12 before
examining a header, and checks the declared length before taking a label slice.
Successful allocation copies at most 10 label bytes. The API cannot retroactively
bound an allocation that its caller made before passing the slice.

The library has no filesystem, network, process, global state or worker effects.
The executable chooses among 14 compiled fictional fixtures and prints only
kind/length metadata or a fixed error code. It accepts no file path. The external
test harness starts bounded local compiler/test processes and removes its owned
temporary directories. Rust toolchain installation is a separate setup step;
the project checks use `--locked --offline` and no external project crates.

The compiler, standard library, allocator and host are trusted components for
this exercise. This is a local parser and CLI contract review, not a deployment
or host-hardening assessment.

## Data model and precedence

`Record` owns a `String` and a copied `Kind`; both fields are private. Safe
accessors return a borrowed label and a copied kind. Parsing performs every
fallible validation before constructing that result. UTF-8 validation precedes
the bounded `to_owned` copy. There is no partial output parameter to mutate.

The refusal order is:

1. more than 12 total bytes;
2. no header;
3. zero declared length;
4. declared length above 10;
5. fewer label bytes than declared;
6. no kind byte after a complete label;
7. trailing bytes after the kind;
8. invalid UTF-8 label;
9. unsupported kind.

The total bound avoids deeper work for oversized inputs. Structural checks then
establish complete, exact slices before content interpretation. For example,
`[11]` is `label-too-long`, while the supplied 13-byte record is `too-large`.
`[1,255,9,0]` is `trailing-data`; removing its last byte yields `invalid-utf8`
before considering kind 9. Equivalent orderings could be designed, but changing
this declared contract requires updating the callers, reading and regressions.

No unsafe block or ABI call is necessary: safe slice operations and UTF-8
validation express the full format. No concurrency is necessary: one bounded
record has no independent work requiring coordination. The unsafe and concurrency
ledgers therefore record no operations and explain those design decisions.

## Before/after claim table

| Claim | Redesign and evidence | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Avoid the demonstrated unchecked input/local-array path | Safe slices, explicit total/declared bounds and no local C buffer; malformed and exact-bound cases pass. | This does not certify the old C function or a future unsafe extension. |
| Preserve the valid format | All three kinds, byte lengths 1 through 10, NUL-containing labels and three-byte Unicode are exercised. | A finite corpus cannot enumerate every UTF-8 label. |
| Own the result | `String` field; `result_owns_label` mutates and drops the source before checking the returned `cat`. | A future borrowed API would need a different lifetime contract. |
| Keep failures distinct and deterministic | Typed variants, the eight supplied cases, combined-fault tests and independent output/status checks. | Business meaning and future grammar changes require review. |
| Bound work inside this parser | Reject more than 12 bytes before content work; at most 10 bytes copied on success. | Caller allocation, toolchain resources and global allocator exhaustion are outside this bound. |
| Avoid diagnostics that expose record contents | CLI emits fixed error codes and valid metadata; expected stderr/stdout are compared exactly. | A future label formatter must define its own escaping/privacy behavior. |
| Reproduce selected observations | Clean rebuilds, locked/offline checks and Git-free packet regression pass. | Tool output is selected evidence, not whole-program security proof. |

## Recorded native and export evidence

[Source revision](https://github.com/instruction-material/Low-Level-Security/tree/5b8ed5bcb87702644e8ac277f1f0d1467fee005d/RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone)
and [CI run](https://github.com/instruction-material/Low-Level-Security/actions/runs/39133603746)
identify the observation. The native and exported-packet checks both passed in
job `117693560785`; the independent reader matched all 16 selected committed
source/tool/workflow files against the artifacts without executing their programs.

- Native compiler: Rust 1.97.1, Edition 2024. Cargo is 1.97.1. The manifests
  declare `record_hardening_lab` 1.0.0 with no dependency section, and each lock
  contains only that local package. This is the dependency review result, not
  an advisory scan of the Rust distribution or a claim of no vulnerabilities.
- Format and warning-denying Clippy passed for both roles. Seven starter and
  thirteen reference library tests passed, then passed again after cleaning
  and rebuilding. That is 40 recorded library-test results per context.
- Fourteen named cases ran twice per role. A clean `cat` run added one per role,
  for 58 exact CLI observations. Twenty usage refusals include non-UTF-8 arguments.
- The independent corpus has 410 distinct vectors per role. It combines all
  strings of 0 through 4 bytes over `{0,1,3,255}`, valid labels over NUL/ASCII
  bytes for lengths 1 through 10 and each kind, and the supplied/additional cases.
  A local consumer exercised the public API and emitted 820 compared results.
- A plain exported packet repeated all 102 native commands without a Git
  repository or Git subprocess. The checkout run had 105 commands, including
  its three Git identity/inventory commands. Exported proofs leave checkout
  identity null and declare only the base pin and exact file hashes.
- Checkout mode refused to claim provenance in the Git-free packet. Native and
  export checkers also refused modified README bytes before running Rust, then
  restored the owned fixture. Neither refusal produced successful evidence.
- Native artifact ZIP SHA-256:
  `33caa353a09ac6793342ff3906002bb2e6ec6b23123cf5973a67f2b65e19bfb7`.
  Export artifact ZIP SHA-256:
  `28f968577cfa8dc3762adde7adf5ae469fde06dd25bf82530359f1c27aaa4dfe`.

This record uses deterministic native cases. It contains no capstone Miri run,
random-fuzz result or ABI adapter, and makes no claim that those ran.

## Five-minute reproduction packet

From the selected `solution` Cargo folder with the recorded toolchain available:

```sh
cargo fmt --all --check
cargo clippy --locked --offline --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --locked --offline
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case cat
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case unicode
cargo run --locked --offline -- --case combined
```

The first three commands return 0; library tests report 13 passed. The two valid
runs print `kind=1 label-bytes=3` and `kind=2 label-bytes=3` on stdout and return
0. The last run returns 65, writes only `error=trailing-data` on stderr and has
empty stdout. Run that expected refusal separately in shells that stop on error.
`result_owns_label` covers mutation/drop of the input, and
`trailing_before_encoding_and_kind` covers combined-fault precedence.

An optional extension may mutate the fixed corpus under the README's explicit
4096-case, 13-byte and 30-second limits; record a new result if doing so. The
provided evidence is the fixed corpus above. Preserve the original lock and
fixture arrays for a clean comparison and retain the command output/statuses.

## Residual-risk analysis

These observations support this format and implementation at the recorded
revision. They do not prove every input, future compiler, allocator behavior,
availability, operational access control or a later extension. Even a bounded
owned-label allocation can fail if the host allocator is exhausted. Future
dependencies need their own lock/advisory review. Any future unsafe/FFI or
concurrent extension must introduce and validate its separate contract rather
than inheriting a security claim from this safe single-record parser.

.github/workflows/rust-capstone.yml.content:
name: Rust record hardening capstone evidence

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_capstone.py"
      - "test/verify_rust_capstone_export.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-capstone.yml"
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone/**"
      - "test/verify_rust_capstone.py"
      - "test/verify_rust_capstone_export.py"
      - ".github/workflows/rust-capstone.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  verify-capstone:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN: "1.97.1"
      SOURCE_REVISION: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install the recorded native toolchain
        run: rustup toolchain install 1.97.1 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
      - name: Compile and verify both capstone roles
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_capstone.py --proof output/rust-capstone-native/proof.json
      - name: Retain exact formatter output on failure
        if: failure()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for role in starter solution; do
            for source in RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone/"$role"/src/*.rs; do
              relative="${source#RUST-10-record-hardening-capstone/}"
              destination="output/rust-capstone-native/formatting/$relative"
              mkdir -p "$(dirname "$destination")"
              rustfmt --edition 2024 --emit stdout "$source" > "$destination"
            done
          done
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-capstone-native-evidence
          path: output/rust-capstone-native/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Repeat the native checks on a plain source export
        run: python3 test/verify_rust_capstone_export.py --proof output/rust-capstone-exported/proof.json
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a
        if: always()
        with:
          name: rust-capstone-exported-evidence
          path: output/rust-capstone-exported/
          include-hidden-files: true
          if-no-files-found: warn
